newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer rejects French plan on ECB control.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer rejects French plan on ECB control.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer on Friday rejected a French proposal for a political counterweight to the future European Central Bank.
Speaking in the northern German city of Muenster, Tietmeyer said the creation of such a body was not in line with the provisions of the Maastricht Treaty on monetary union.

In a clear reference to comments by French president Jacques Chirac, Tietmeyer used the French phrases "pouvoir politique" -- political power -- and "pouvoir monetaire" monetary power, according to the text of his speech.
"Any attempts to create a 'pouvoir politique' to control or influence the 'pouvoir monetaire' would not be in line with the Treaty," Tietmeyer said.
"I hope that this will ultimately also be seen this way even in countries that do not have a similarly long tradition of an independent central bank," he added.
The Maastricht Treaty calls clearly for an independent central bank, which is entirely free from political influence and has price stability as its main priority.

Tietmeyer also warned against the precept of accepting a moderate increase in inflation if this allowed an interest rate cut which could stimulate growth, cut joblessness, help the welfare system and find answers to globalisation.
"Too low interest rates and a little more inflation are never a solution for this, neither today nor tomorrow," he said.
